mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 5% increase in HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points in the last month signals an improving labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 0.2pp decrease in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months indicates a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 1% increase in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over the last three months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 2% increase in CPIAUCSL (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the last two months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals a strengthening consumer demand and improving labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 2 months AND UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following the combined increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher in periods following a 200,000 increase in PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly lower in periods following a 1% decrease in GDPC1 (t-test p > 0.05).
